intentions: Arc 1, episode 1 of 5. Maya calls Ron to a rooftop greenhouse where a night watchman lies dead in a room locked from the inside; every plant has wilted except one orchid. Ron sees the room differently from the police. Moss waits quietly at the door.

Arc 1, episode 2 of 5. Ron imagines three ways the room could have been sealed and rules out two. Arjun's client, the greenhouse owner, asks Ron for help, which puts Arjun and Maya on different sides of the same door.

Arc 1, episode 3 of 5. Ron builds a confident theory that the watchman was poisoned through the watering system. It satisfies everyone, but it cannot explain why one orchid lived, and it points at the wrong person.

Arc 1, episode 4 of 5. A university student who earns money delivering plants mentions a plain detail about how the greenhouse timer is set. It breaks Ron's theory. He admits the gap and starts again.

Arc 1, episode 5 of 5. Ron rebuilds the case from the student's detail and names the real cause and the real person; Maya makes the arrest. In the owner's papers Ron finds a name he recognises, and he does not tell anyone yet.

Arc 2, episode 1 of 5. The name leads Ron to a quiet woman in a small flat. He recognises it from the case that ended his time with the police, and tells Arjun and Maya what he has never told them together.
Arc 2, episode 2 of 5. Ron and Maya walk back through the old case. They remember it differently: what Ron imagined then, and what Maya could not stand behind. Moss stays close to Ron.
Arc 2, episode 3 of 5. Ron's old reconstruction has a gap he never saw. A baker who opens at four in the morning mentions what he saw on his daily round, and it fits the gap exactly.
Arc 2, episode 4 of 5. Arjun finds the legal way in: the old file was never properly closed. Ron must decide whether to reopen it and risk Maya's position in the police.

Arc 2, episode 5 of 5. Ron and Maya reach what really happened. What Ron imagined was right in its shape and wrong in one detail. He makes peace with it. A small brass object recovered from the old case is left in his hands, and he does not know whose it was.
Arc 3, episode 1 of 5. A woman brings Ron a brass compass with a cracked lid that her late father left her. The needle points a few degrees wrong, and she wants to know why her father kept it.
Arc 3, episode 2 of 5. Ron imagines the compass's history. Maya checks the records and finds it listed in an unsolved theft. Arjun warns the woman that owning it may put her in trouble.
Arc 3, episode 3 of 5. Ron decides the error is deliberate and that the needle points to a hiding place. He follows it and is wrong about where.

Arc 3, episode 4 of 5. A cleaner who works the night shift at the ferry terminal explains something ordinary about the metal in the building, and the error in the needle makes sense. Ron corrects himself.

Arc 3, episode 5 of 5. The compass leads to what the father hid and why. Ron decides what happens to the object. It stays with the woman, and Ron writes down what he learned from it so the story can return to it.
purpose: Three five-episode arcs: a striking unusual crime (the greenhouse), Ron's own background through a case that reaches into his past, and a case built around one small object (the brass compass) that the story will remember. In every arc an ordinary person doing an ordinary job supplies the plain fact that makes the truth click.
